To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrical conductivity of the nanocomposites is almost independent of compressive loading.
the resistivity of epoxy graphene and carbon nanofiber composites is almost independent of compressive stress.
the electrical conductivity of graphene/epoxy composites under compressive load is almost independent of the applied compressive stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
electrical properties of epoxy based nanomaterials containing graphene and carbon nanofibres, under compressive load.
the study of electrical properties of epoxy based nanomaterials containing graphene flakes and/or carbon nano fibers.
the electrical conductivity of nanocomposite materials containing carbon nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stress dependence is induced by formation microcracks and debonding of graphene flakes.
the electrical conductivity of the composite is determined only by the level of tensiles stresses in the composite and not by compressive stresses.
the electrical resistivity of epoxy graphene and carbon nanofibres composites is a function of the tensile stress only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrical conductivity is a function of tensile stress only.
the electrical conductivity of the nanocomposites is not sensitive to compressive loading and is only sensitive to the level of tensil stress.
the electrical conductivity of the nanocomposites depends on the tensile stress in a material, but is independent of the compressing one.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrical conductivity of the composites is not sensitive to the compressive stress, and thus the compressive strength of the composites can be determined by conventional methods, e.g. using a compression test.
the compressive loading of the epoxy graphene and epoxy nano fibers composites has negligible influence on the overall resistivity.
electrical conductivity of epoxy graphene composites is not a reliable indicator of the material integrity.
